rest.matching.answers.malformed: Any endpoint, when the query string is not valid URL encoding or UTF-8, and any request with a body (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`) whose body does not parse as its `Content-Type` says: malformed JSON, or a broken form or multipart body. Any other `Content-Type` is accepted and its body ignored, so matching never answers `415`. Nothing was read or changed; fix the request before sending it again.
rest.matching.answers.unauthorized: Any endpoint, when the token got past the gateway but matching refuses it: no `Authorization` header reached matching, or more than one; the header is not exactly `Bearer <token>`; the token is not an access token (a refresh or two-factor challenge token); it was issued for another issuer or audience, has expired, or is signed with a key identity no longer publishes; or it lacks `sub`, `email` or `role`. Sign in again, or exchange the refresh token, and retry.
rest.matching.answers.notAdmin: Every endpoint except `GET /api/v1/matching/driver/me`, when the token's `role` is not `admin`. `message` names the caller's role; the same token always gets the same answer.
rest.matching.answers.noRoute: Any path under `/api/v1/matching` that matching has no route for, and any method a path does not take: Phoenix answers `404` for both, never `405`. Check the method and the path.
rest.matching.answers.notAcceptable: Any endpoint, when the `Accept` header names neither a JSON type nor `*/*`, or the query carries a `_format` other than `json`. Send `Accept: application/json`, or no `Accept` header.
rest.matching.answers.tooLarge: Any request with a body (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`), when the body is larger than 8,000,000 bytes of JSON or multipart, or 1,000,000 bytes of URL-encoded form. No endpoint here takes more than a few bytes.
rest.matching.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when something fails that matching did not expect. `traceId` is the id matching gave the request: its `X-Request-Id`, which Kong sets when the client sends none, or a new id when that one is shorter than 20 or longer than 200 characters. Quote it when reporting the failure. As the body says, the request may have taken effect before it failed: before repeating a `POST`, read the job with `GET /api/v1/matching/backoffice/dispatches/{id}`. An `assign` that fails while the assignment is being written leaves the job `pending` and the courier it picked free.
rest.matching.answers.database: `GET /api/v1/matching/driver/me` and every endpoint under `/api/v1/matching/backoffice`, when matching cannot reach its database or the database does not answer in time. Retry later; before repeating a `POST`, read the job first. An `assign` cut off this way leaves the courier it picked free for other work.
rest.matching.answers.identityUnavailabl: Any endpoint, when the token is signed with a key matching has not loaded yet and identity's key set cannot be fetched; after 3 failed fetches in a row matching stops asking for 5 seconds. Tokens signed with a key it already holds are not affected. Nothing was read or changed; retry later.
rest.matching.driverMe.summary: The caller's own courier record: the vehicle this account drives and whether it may work. The courier app reads it after signing in, for the `id` it joins the driver socket with.
rest.matching.driverMe.who: Any signed-in account; only an account with an approved courier record gets `200`.
rest.matching.driverMe.case.found: The account has an approved courier record. `id` is the driver id: join the driver socket topic `driver:<id>` with it. `status` is the live duty status, `offline` when matching is not tracking the courier right now.
rest.matching.driverMe.case.pendingAppro: The account has a courier record that an administrator has not approved yet. The driver socket refuses it too; ask again after approval.
rest.matching.driverMe.case.noDriverReco: The account has no courier record in matching: it is another role, or its courier registration has not reached matching.
rest.matching.listDrivers.summary: Every courier matching tracks live right now, with the last position each one reported. Read from memory, not the database.
rest.matching.listDrivers.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.listDrivers.case.listed: The couriers tracked live, in no particular order. A courier who has not connected since matching started, or has been offline with no connection for 15 minutes, is not listed. `coordinates` is `null` until the courier has sent a position; `recorded_at` is when the phone took it, and `updated_at` when matching last changed this courier's state.
rest.matching.nearbyDrivers.summary: Tracked couriers within a radius of a point, nearest first, whatever their duty status.
rest.matching.nearbyDrivers.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.nearbyDrivers.field.latitu: Decimal degrees from `-90` to `90`, such as `-6.1754`; the whole value must be a number. Missing, out of range, not a number (`-6.2abc`), or a list or map (`latitude[]=…`): `400` `invalid_nearby_query`.
rest.matching.nearbyDrivers.field.longit: Decimal degrees from `-180` to `180`, such as `106.8272`; the whole value must be a number. Missing, out of range, not a number (`106.8east`), or a list or map (`longitude[]=…`): `400` `invalid_nearby_query`.
rest.matching.nearbyDrivers.field.radius: Kilometres, above `0`; `3.0` when absent. The whole value must be a number (`3km` is refused). Not a number, `0` or less, or a list or map: `400` `invalid_nearby_query`.
rest.matching.nearbyDrivers.case.found: Couriers whose last position lies within `radius_km` of the point, nearest first, each with `distance_km` rounded to 3 decimals. Couriers with no position yet are left out; an empty `data` means nobody is in range.
rest.matching.nearbyDrivers.case.invalid: `latitude` or `longitude` is missing; a value is not a number from its first character to its last, or is a list or a map; `latitude` lies outside `-90` to `90` or `longitude` outside `-180` to `180`; or `radius_km` is not above `0`. Nothing was read; correct the query.
rest.matching.getDriver.summary: One courier's live state, by driver id.
rest.matching.getDriver.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.getDriver.field.id: The driver id, a positive integer, as the courier list and the jobs show it.
rest.matching.getDriver.case.found: The courier is tracked live; the fields are those of `GET /api/v1/matching/drivers`.
rest.matching.getDriver.case.notTracked: No courier with this id is tracked right now: the id is unknown, the courier has not connected since matching started, or has been offline with no connection for 15 minutes.
rest.matching.listDispatches.summary: The dispatch board: fleet jobs, newest first, one page at a time.
rest.matching.listDispatches.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.listDispatches.field.statu: One of `pending`, `assigned`, `picked_up`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, or `all`, the default. Anything else: `400` `invalid_status`.
rest.matching.listDispatches.field.limit: Jobs per page, `1` to `200`; `50` when absent. Anything else: `400` `invalid_limit`.
rest.matching.listDispatches.field.befor: A job id: only jobs with a smaller id come back. Send the previous page's `next_cursor`. Not a positive integer: `400` `invalid_cursor`.
rest.matching.listDispatches.case.page: One page, by `id` descending. Send `next_cursor` as `before` for the next page; it is `null` on the last one. `pickup` and `dropoff` are the points order gave when it asked for a courier, `weight_kg` is the parcel's weight rounded up to whole kilograms, and `driver_id` and `assigned_at` are `null` while a job is `pending`.
rest.matching.listDispatches.case.invali: `status` is neither a job status nor `all`.
`limit` is not an integer from `1` to `200`.
rest.matching.dispatchSummary.summary: The counts at the head of the dispatch board.
rest.matching.dispatchSummary.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.dispatchSummary.case.count: `pending` counts jobs waiting for a courier, `active` every job not yet delivered or cancelled (`pending` ones included), and `delivered_today` the jobs delivered since midnight in the platform's time zone.
rest.matching.getDispatch.summary: One fleet job, with its proof of delivery.
rest.matching.getDispatch.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.getDispatch.field.id: The job id, a positive integer, as the dispatch board shows it.
rest.matching.getDispatch.case.found: The job. `proof_of_delivery.photo_url` is a link that reads the photo for 15 minutes; fetch the job again for a fresh one. `signature` is the courier's drawing as a `data:image/png;base64,` URI. Both are `null` until the job is delivered.
rest.matching.assignDispatch.summary: Gives a waiting job to a courier the administrator chooses, instead of the nearest one. The choice overrides what automatic dispatch checks: the courier's capacity and how recent their last position is are not checked here. Matching records every request on its administrator routes with the administrator's account and the outcome.
rest.matching.assignDispatch.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.assignDispatch.field.id: The job id, a positive integer.
rest.matching.assignDispatch.field.drive: The courier's driver id: a positive JSON integer or a string of digits. Also read from the query string. Missing: `400` `driver_id_required`; not a positive integer: `400` `invalid_id`.
rest.matching.assignDispatch.case.assign: The job is `assigned` to the courier, whose app receives `order_assigned` on the driver socket. The courier counts as busy until the job is delivered, cancelled or taken off them.
rest.matching.assignDispatch.case.invali: `id` or `driver_id` is not a positive integer.
rest.matching.assignDispatch.case.alread: The job is not `pending`: it already has a courier, or it is delivered or cancelled. To give it to another courier, unassign it first.
rest.matching.assignDispatch.case.driver: The courier exists but matching is not tracking them live: they have not connected since matching started, or have been offline with no connection for 15 minutes.
The courier is tracked but not `online`: off duty, or already carrying a job; a courier carries one job at a time.
rest.matching.unassignDispatch.summary: Takes an assigned job off its courier and returns it to `pending`. Matching then offers it again, within about a second, to the nearest available courier within 3 km of the pickup other than the one it was taken from, or as soon as one comes on duty.
rest.matching.unassignDispatch.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.unassignDispatch.field.id: The job id, a positive integer.
rest.matching.unassignDispatch.case.unas: The job is `pending` again, with `driver_id` and `assigned_at` `null`. The courier's app receives `order_unassigned`, then `active_order`, and the courier is free for other work. Automatic dispatch never offers this job to that courier again; an administrator can still give it to them with `assign`. Order is not told: the order number and the waybill stay on the job.
rest.matching.unassignDispatch.case.notA: The job is `pending`: no courier holds it.
rest.matching.unassignDispatch.case.inva: The job is `picked_up`, `delivered` or `cancelled`. A picked-up parcel is in the courier's hands and stays with them.
rest.matching.cancelDispatch.summary: Cancels a fleet job that was not booked for an order. Matching refuses to cancel any job that carries an order number.
rest.matching.cancelDispatch.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.cancelDispatch.field.id: The job id, a positive integer.
rest.matching.cancelDispatch.case.cancel: The job is `cancelled`; a courier who held it is freed and receives `order_updated`. Cancelling a job already `cancelled` gives the same answer and changes nothing.
rest.matching.cancelDispatch.case.boundT: The job carries an `order_number`, as every job order books does. Order would never hear of a cancellation made here, and its paid order would wait for a courier forever, so matching refuses whatever the job's status.
rest.matching.cancelDispatch.case.invali: The job has no order number but is `picked_up` or `delivered`: a parcel in a courier's hands, or delivered, is not cancelled.
rest.matching.driverDispatches.summary: The jobs a courier holds now, `assigned` and `picked_up`, most recently assigned first.
rest.matching.driverDispatches.who: Administrators only (`role` `admin`), and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Any other role gets `403`, listed in matching's answers.
rest.matching.driverDispatches.field.dri: The courier's driver id, a positive integer.
rest.matching.driverDispatches.case.list: The courier's open jobs. An unknown `driver_id` gets an empty `data`, not `404`.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.summary: Puts the proof-of-delivery photo straight into object storage, at the address matching signed in its reply to the driver socket's `pod_upload`. Matching is not called: the signature in the query is the permission, and it covers the host, the two headers below and the time.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.who: Whoever holds the address: the courier carrying the job, who asked for it with `pod_upload` while the job was `picked_up`.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.field.buc: Part of `upload_url`; send the URL unchanged, never build it.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.field.dis: The job id the address was signed for.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.field.sha: The photo's SHA-256 in lowercase hex: the `photo_sha256` sent with `pod_upload`.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.field.xAm: When matching signed the address, from `upload_url`.
`600`: the address works for 600 seconds after `X-Amz-Date`.
`host;if-none-match;x-amz-checksum-sha256`, from `upload_url`: the headers the signature covers.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.field.hos: The host of `upload_url`, unchanged; the signature covers it.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.field.ifN: Exactly `*`, from `upload_headers`. Signed: leaving it out or changing it breaks the signature. It makes the store refuse a second write to the same key.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.field.xAm: The base64 of the photo's SHA-256 digest, exactly as in `upload_headers`. Signed; the store refuses bytes with another digest.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.field.pho: The JPEG itself: exactly the bytes hashed for `photo_sha256`. At `delivered` matching checks that the stored object begins as a JPEG does (`FF D8 FF`).
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.case.stor: The store kept the photo. Send `delivered` on the driver socket with `photo_url` from the `pod_upload` reply as `pod_photo_url`.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.case.badD: The SHA-256 of the bytes sent is not the one in `x-amz-checksum-sha256`: the store answers S3's `BadDigest` and keeps nothing. Hash exactly the bytes you send, ask for a new address with `pod_upload`, and upload again.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.case.sign: The signature does not hold: the URL was altered, the request went to another host, a signed header was left out or changed (some stores answer `400` for a missing one), or more than 600 seconds have passed since `X-Amz-Date`. Nothing is stored; ask for a new address with `pod_upload`.
rest.matching.uploadProofPhoto.case.alre: An object already exists under this key. The key names the photo's own SHA-256, so these bytes were uploaded before and the first copy stays: go on to `delivered`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.summary: Matching's driver socket: one WebSocket that the courier app keeps open while the courier works, carrying Phoenix channel frames. On it the app joins `driver:<driver id>`, declares duty, sends positions, receives the job matching assigns, and reports the pickup and the delivery. Kong passes the upgrade to matching without looking at the token; matching checks it once, during the upgrade, so an open socket outlives its token and every new connection needs a current one. matching closes a socket that has sent nothing for 60 seconds. Every handshake answer carries `x-request-id`, the id matching gave the request.
rest.matching.driverSocket.who: An approved courier: the token's `role` is `courier` or `admin`, and matching holds an approved courier record for its `sub`. The socket belongs to that record's driver id, the only `driver:` topic it may join.
rest.matching.driverSocket.field.vsn: The frame format. `2.0.0` selects the JSON arrays `[join_ref, ref, topic, event, payload]` shown here. Without `vsn` Phoenix speaks `1.0.0`, JSON objects, which this reference does not describe. A value that is not a version, or matches neither `1.0.x` nor `2.0.x`, is refused `403`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.field.secWebS: Two subprotocols, comma-separated: `phoenix`, then `base64url.bearer.phx.` followed by the access token encoded in base64. An access token is made of letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, so its base64 holds only letters and digits and reads the same in the standard and the URL-safe alphabet; the `=` padding may be dropped, as the courier app does. Always name `phoenix`: matching answers `101` with it, and refuses `403` a header that names another subprotocol but not `phoenix`. Send exactly one token entry: with two, matching reads no token.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.upgraded: matching accepted the token and found the approved courier record. `sec-websocket-protocol: phoenix` names the subprotocol it selected. Join `driver:<driver id>` next, then send a frame at least every 60 seconds.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.notUpgra: A `GET` whose token matching accepted, but which is not a WebSocket upgrade: no `Upgrade: websocket`, no `Sec-WebSocket-Key`, or a `Sec-WebSocket-Version` other than `13`. The body names the first header at fault. A WebSocket library never sends such a request.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.unreadab: The `base64url.bearer.phx.` entry is not base64 that both the standard and the URL-safe alphabet read: it holds a character other than letters, digits and a trailing `=`, such as `+`, `/`, `-` or `_`, or its length is impossible. Encode the access token again; the same header always gets this answer.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.origin: The request carries an `Origin` whose host is not `api.wildanfrananda.my.id`, as a browser page on another host sends. Mobile apps send no `Origin`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.noPhoeni: `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` names a subprotocol besides the token entry, but not `phoenix`. Name `phoenix` beside the token entry.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.version: `vsn` is not a version, or matches neither `1.0.x` nor `2.0.x`. Send `vsn=2.0.0`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.tokenRef: matching read no token, or refused the one it read: no `base64url.bearer.phx.` entry, or two of them; a token that is not an access token, has expired, was issued for another issuer or audience, or is signed with a key identity does not publish; or a token without `sub`, `email` or `role`. Renew the session with the refresh token and connect again.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.notCouri: The token's `role` is neither `courier` nor `admin`. Sign in with a courier account.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.noCourie: matching holds no approved courier record for the token's `sub`: the courier registration has not reached matching, or an administrator has not approved it yet. `GET /api/v1/matching/driver/me` tells the two apart: `404` `no_driver_record` or `403` `pending_approval`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.identity: The token is signed with a key matching has not loaded, and identity's key set could not be fetched; after 3 failed fetches in a row matching stops asking for 5 seconds. Tokens signed with a key it already holds are not affected. Connect again after a pause.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.internal: Something matching did not expect failed during the upgrade, for example its token verifier did not answer. No socket was opened. `traceId` is the id matching gave the request, also in `x-request-id`; quote it when reporting the failure, and connect again after a pause.
rest.matching.driverSocket.case.database: matching could not reach its database, or it did not answer in time, while looking up the courier record. No socket was opened; connect again after a pause. `traceId` is the id matching gave the request, also in `x-request-id`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.join.summary: Joins the courier's channel: `driver:` followed by the driver id, the `id` of `GET /api/v1/matching/driver/me`. The payload is ignored; send `{}`. Every later frame on this topic carries the join's `ref` as its `join_ref`; a frame with another `join_ref` than that or `null` is dropped without a reply. Phoenix answers `unmatched topic` to a join whose topic does not begin with `driver:`, and to any frame on a topic that is not joined.
rest.matching.driverSocket.join.reply.jo: The topic names the socket's own driver id. `status` is the courier's duty status, which joining does not change; it is `offline` when the previous channel ended first, because a channel that ends takes the courier off duty. Send `status` `online` after every join to stay on duty. matching pushes `active_order` right after this reply.
rest.matching.driverSocket.join.reply.in: What follows `driver:` is not a positive integer.
rest.matching.driverSocket.join.reply.fo: The driver id in the topic is not the one the socket was opened for. Ask `GET /api/v1/matching/driver/me` for the courier's id.
rest.matching.driverSocket.join.reply.jo: matching failed while joining, for example because its database did not answer. The channel is not joined; join again after a pause.
rest.matching.driverSocket.heartbeat.sum: Keeps the connection alive: matching closes a socket that has sent nothing for 60 seconds. Send it on the topic `phoenix` with `join_ref` `null`, every 30 seconds or so; Phoenix answers it from the socket itself, joined or not.
rest.matching.driverSocket.heartbeat.rep: Always, while the connection is up. A heartbeat without a reply within a few seconds means the connection is gone: close it and connect again.
rest.matching.driverSocket.status.summar: Sets the courier's duty status: `online` makes the courier available for jobs, `offline` takes them off duty. `busy` is what matching sets while the courier holds a job.
The status now in force. After `online` it is `online`, or `busy` when the courier already holds a job; matching assigns jobs only to `online` couriers. After `offline` it is `offline`; a job the courier holds stays theirs.
`status` is missing, or is not `online`, `busy` or `offline`.
`busy` was sent while the courier holds no job.
rest.matching.driverSocket.ping.summary: Reports the courier's newest position. `latitude` (-90 to 90) and `longitude` (-180 to 180) are numbers; `recorded_at` is an ISO 8601 time with its offset, such as `Z`; `speed_kmh` (zero or more) and `bearing_deg` (from 0 up to but not including 360) may be left out. Automatic dispatch considers only couriers whose position arrived after they went `online`, so send one right after `status`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.ping.reply.ac: The position is taken. It becomes the courier's live position, unless it was recorded before the one matching already holds: that one is ignored with the same reply.
rest.matching.driverSocket.ping.reply.in: A field is missing or out of range, `recorded_at` has no offset, or it is more than 300 seconds ahead of matching's clock. Sending the same position again gets the same answer.
rest.matching.driverSocket.ping.reply.ra: More than 100 `ping`s from this courier in 10 seconds. Nothing was recorded; send the newest position after a pause.
rest.matching.driverSocket.pingBatch.sum: Sends positions the phone recorded while it had no connection: at most 100 in `pings`, each shaped like a `ping` payload. matching keeps them as the courier's history; they never move the live position and do not count for dispatch. The batch belongs to the courier the socket was opened for.
rest.matching.driverSocket.pingBatch.rep: The batch was read. Each entry's index in `pings`, counted from 0, is in one list: `stored`, kept now; `duplicates`, its `recorded_at` is already stored for the courier or repeats an earlier entry of the batch; `refused`, with `invalid_telemetry` as for `ping`, `ahead_of_server_clock` for more than 300 seconds ahead, or `too_old` for more than 24 hours old. Sending the batch again is safe: what was stored comes back in `duplicates`, and a refused entry is refused again.
`pings` is missing or not a list.
`pings` holds more than 100 entries. Nothing was stored; split the batch.
More than 30 batches from this courier in 60 seconds. Nothing was stored; send the batch again later.
matching could not store the entries, for example because its database did not answer. Send the same batch again later; entries already stored come back in `duplicates`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.pickup.summar: Reports that the courier has collected the parcel of job `order_id` from the merchant.
The job is `picked_up`, and matching pushes `order_updated` with that status. A `pickup` for a job already `picked_up` gets the same reply and changes nothing, so a push whose reply was lost can be sent again.
`order_id` is missing or not a positive integer; a number written as a string is refused too.
The job is not assigned to this courier: it is another courier's, or nobody's yet.
The job is this courier's but not `assigned`: it is already `delivered`, or it was cancelled.
rest.matching.driverSocket.podUpload.sum: Asks for the address to upload the proof-of-delivery photo to. Hash the JPEG's exact bytes with SHA-256 and send the hash as 64 lowercase hex digits in `photo_sha256`. The job must be `picked_up`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.podUpload.rep: `upload_url` is a presigned `PUT` address on the storage host, valid for 600 seconds: send the photo's bytes to it unchanged, with the headers of `upload_headers` exactly as they are, and no token. `photo_url` is where the photo will be; `delivered` takes it as `pod_photo_url`. Asking again gives a fresh address for the same photo.
`order_id` is missing or not a positive integer. It is checked before anything else.
`photo_sha256` is missing or not 64 lowercase hex digits. It is checked before the job is read.
The job is not assigned to this courier.
The job is not `picked_up`: send `pickup` first, or the job is already delivered or cancelled.
rest.matching.driverSocket.delivered.sum: Reports the delivery with its proof. `pod_photo_url` is `photo_url` from `pod_upload`, once the photo is uploaded; `pod_signature` is the receiver's signature as a PNG in a `data:image/png;base64,` URI. Both are required. Before it accepts, matching reads the stored photo: it must be in this job's folder, carry the checksum its name promises, and begin as a JPEG does.
rest.matching.driverSocket.delivered.rep: The job is `delivered`, and matching pushes `order_updated` with that status; for a job that belongs to an order, matching then reports the delivery to order by itself. A `delivered` for a job already `delivered` gets the same reply and changes nothing, so a push whose reply was lost can be sent again.
`order_id` is missing or not a positive integer.
The job is not assigned to this courier.
The job is neither `picked_up` nor `delivered`: it has not been picked up yet, or it was cancelled.
`pod_signature` is missing, empty or not a string.

The proof does not hold: the signature is not a PNG in a `data:image/png;base64,` URI with padded base64, or is longer than 65,536 characters; `pod_photo_url` is missing or is not the `photo_url` of a photo of this job; or the photo is not stored, carries another checksum, or does not begin as a JPEG does. Nothing was recorded.
matching could not reach storage to check the photo. Nothing was recorded; send `delivered` again.
rest.matching.driverSocket.activeOrder.s: The courier's current job: the newest that is `assigned` or `picked_up`, in the shape of `order_assigned`, or `null` in `order` when there is none. matching pushes it right after every join and after `order_unassigned`; use it to resume a job after reconnecting.
rest.matching.driverSocket.orderAssigned: A job was just assigned to this courier: automatically, to the nearest `online` courier whose position arrived since going on duty and whose vehicle can carry the weight, or by an administrator. There is no offer to accept or decline. `id` is the `order_id` that `pickup`, `pod_upload` and `delivered` send; `weight_kg` is in whole kilograms.
This courier's job changed status: `picked_up` after `pickup`, `delivered` after `delivered`, or `cancelled` when an administrator cancelled it. Same shape as `order_assigned`.
rest.matching.driverSocket.orderUnassign: An administrator took job `id` off this courier: it is `pending` again and may go to another courier, but never automatically back to this one. `active_order` follows.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.summary: Matching's merchant socket, which the seller web opens through the edge on its own host: one WebSocket carrying Phoenix channel frames. On it the page joins `merchant:<principalId>` and hears about the seller's courier jobs: `active_orders` right after the join, then `order_updated` for every change. The browser sends its session cookie and holds no token: the edge checks the session and its role, then opens matching's socket through the gateway with the session's access token, which never reaches the browser. The Phoenix JavaScript client given `/bff/ws/v1/matching/merchant` opens `/bff/ws/v1/matching/merchant/websocket`; the edge serves both. matching closes a socket that has sent nothing for 60 seconds. Every handshake answer from matching carries `x-request-id`, the id it gave the request.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.who: A seller: the session's role must be `seller`, and the edge refuses an applicant's `customer` session. matching admits the token's `seller` role, and the only topic the socket may join is `merchant:` followed by the session's `principalId`.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.field.vsn: The frame format, passed to matching unchanged. `2.0.0` selects the JSON arrays `[join_ref, ref, topic, event, payload]` shown here, and is what the Phoenix JavaScript client sends. Without `vsn` Phoenix speaks `1.0.0`, JSON objects, which this reference does not describe. A value that is not a version, or matches neither `1.0.x` nor `2.0.x`, is refused `403`.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.field.secWe: Offer `phoenix`, or nothing: the Phoenix JavaScript client offers nothing when it has no `authToken`, and the page never has one. The edge does not pass the page's offer on but offers matching its own, with the session's access token, so a token entry here is ignored. The `101` names `phoenix` only when the page offered it; to any other offer it names none, and the browser then fails the connection.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.upgrad: The edge found a live seller session, and matching accepted the access token the edge sent for it; the answer carries no token and no cookie. `sec-websocket-protocol: phoenix` is there only when the page offered `phoenix`. Join `merchant:<principalId>` next, then send a frame at least every 60 seconds.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.sessio: The browser sent no usable `__Host-kx_session` cookie: none at all, a malformed value, or the cookie twice. Nothing was opened. Show the sign-in, and open the socket after it.

The cookie names no live session: its limits passed, it was signed out, a newer sign-in or sign-up in this browser replaced it, or identity refused to renew its tokens. Nothing was opened, and the answer expires the cookie. Show the sign-in, and open the socket after it.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.csrfRe: `Origin` is missing, or is not exactly `https://seller.wildanfrananda.my.id`: the upgrade did not come from the seller web's own page. Other `GET` requests through the edge are not checked, but the upgrade needs `Origin`, which a browser always sends. Nothing was opened, and the session is untouched.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.roleRe: The session's access token had less than 60 seconds left, and the pair identity issued to renew it says the account is neither `seller` nor `customer` any more. The session has ended and the answer expires the cookie; show the sign-in.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.seller: The session is an applicant's: its role is `customer`. Nothing was opened, and the session stays signed in. An account approved since the session last received tokens is still `customer` here until the edge renews them; signing in again gives it the `seller` role at once.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.versio: matching refused the frame version: `vsn` is not a version, or matches neither `1.0.x` nor `2.0.x`. The edge passes the empty refusal on. Send `vsn=2.0.0`.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.tokenR: matching did not accept the access token the edge sent for the session, for example because identity has just begun signing with a key matching has not loaded: matching fetches identity's key set again at most once every 10 seconds. The edge passes the empty refusal on, and the session is unchanged. Open the socket again after a few seconds.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.websoc: The request is not a WebSocket upgrade: `Upgrade` is not `websocket`, `Connection` does not list `upgrade`, `Sec-WebSocket-Key` is missing, or `Sec-WebSocket-Version` is not `13`. A browser's `WebSocket` never sends such a request; a plain `fetch` of the path gets this answer.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.intern: Something matching did not expect failed while it checked the token, for example its token verifier did not answer. Nothing was opened, and the edge passes the answer on. `traceId` is the id matching gave the request, also in `x-request-id`; quote it when reporting the failure, and open the socket again after a pause.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.storeU: The edge could not reach its session store, or the store refused a read or a write, so nothing was checked and nothing was opened. The cookie is unchanged; open the socket again after a pause.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.identi: The session's access token had less than 60 seconds left, and the edge could not renew it now: identity could not be reached or answered with a failure, or another request of the session was renewing it and did not finish in time. Nothing was opened and the session stays; open the socket again after a pause.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.apiUna: The edge could not reach the gateway, or the gateway did not answer the upgrade within 90 seconds. Nothing was opened; open the socket again after a pause. When the gateway is reached but matching is not, the gateway's own answer comes back instead.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.case.keysUn: The token is signed with a key matching has not loaded, and identity's key set could not be fetched; after 3 failed fetches in a row matching stops asking for 5 seconds. The edge passes the empty refusal on. Open the socket again after a pause.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.join.summar: Joins the seller's channel: `merchant:` followed by the session's `principalId`, from `GET /bff/session`. The payload is ignored; send `{}`. The channel only pushes: any other event the page sends on it is answered `{"status": "error", "response": {"reason": "unknown_event"}}`, and the channel stays joined. Every later frame on this topic carries the join's `ref` as its `join_ref`. Phoenix answers `unmatched topic` to a join whose topic does not begin with `merchant:`, and to any frame on a topic that is not joined.
The topic names the session's own principal. matching pushes `active_orders` right after this reply, then `order_updated` whenever one of the seller's jobs changes.
What follows `merchant:` is empty, or longer than 64 characters, once spaces at either end are removed.
The principal in the topic is not the session's. Take `principalId` from `GET /bff/session`.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.heartbeat.s: Keeps the connection alive: matching closes a socket that has sent nothing for 60 seconds. Send it on the topic `phoenix` with `join_ref` `null`, every 30 seconds or so; the Phoenix JavaScript client does this by itself. Phoenix answers it from the socket itself, joined or not.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.heartbeat.r: Always, while the connection is up. A heartbeat without a reply within a few seconds means the connection is gone: close it and connect again.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.activeOrder: The seller's unfinished jobs, `pending`, `assigned` or `picked_up`, oldest first, in `orders`; an empty list when there are none. Each has the shape of `order_updated`. matching pushes it once, right after each join: take it as the current state after every reconnect, since changes made while the socket was down are not sent again.
rest.matching.merchantSocket.orderUpdate: One of the seller's jobs was booked or changed. matching books a job when order asks for a courier for a packed parcel: it starts `pending`, already with its `awb_number`, the tracking number on the shipping label; it becomes `assigned`, with `driver_id` and `assigned_at`, when a courier is assigned to it, `pending` again if an administrator takes it off the courier, then `picked_up`, and `delivered` with `delivered_at`. `order_number` names the order; `weight_kg` is in whole kilograms.
